title: Redwood / HeliosHealth Security & Privacy Review
summary: Security and privacy deep-dive focused on data handling, retention, PII/PHI protections, KMS/encryption, and confirmation that customer data is not used for model training. Discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and residency. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 report, KMS integration guide, data flow diagram, and schedule a technical pilot for ingestion and redaction checks.
transcript: [00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone good afternoon thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes on the agenda — quick intros then we'll jump into security and data handling details.
[00:12] Taylor (HeliosHealth): Hi all Taylor here — Head of Security at HeliosHealth. We're mainly focused on how you handle PHI, retention, and contractual guarantees around training data.
[00:23] Priya (HeliosHealth): Priya, CTO — I'll be listening for integration constraints (VPC, KMS) and latency implications of any encryption flow.
[00:34] Alex (Redwood): Great. Samir and Jordan from our security engineering team are here to cover the nuts and bolts — Samir over to you for cert posture.

[00:42] Samir (Redwood): Thanks — quick note: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in prod, pursuing ISO 27001; I'll share the cert pack after the call. Our control scope covers hosted API and dedicated offerings — private deployments have separate attestations. (small pause)
[01:05] Marcus (HeliosHealth): Is the SOC 2 report for the current infra or only for the hosted tenant? we need clarity for Dedicated vs Hosted.

[01:12] Samir (Redwood): Good question. The SOC 2 covers our hosted and dedicated control plane. For private (VPC/on-prem) we provide enterprise package and there's a distinct set of controls; we can provide letters and architecture diagrams for that.
[01:28] Riley (HeliosHealth): On SSO — we use Okta. Are you supporting SAML and OIDC for RBAC/SCIM provisioning?

[01:35] Jordan (Redwood): Yes Okta works. We support SAML SSO and OIDC flows, and SCIM for user/group provisioning. RBAC is role-based with customizable roles; audit logs capture role changes and admin actions.
[01:48] Taylor (HeliosHealth): Audit logs — retention and access model? we need at least one year and exportability to our SIEM.

[01:55] Samir (Redwood): Default retention is 90 days in the console, but for enterprise we can configure log archival to S3 for 12+ months and provide streaming to customer SIEM (syslog/Kinesis). We'll share the log schema.

[02:20] Priya (HeliosHealth): Okay. Now the critical piece: prompts and content retention. We need to know what is persisted, for how long, and whether Redwood uses any customer prompts or outputs for model training or improvement.
[02:34] Alex (Redwood): Short answer: we don't train on customer data. Let me hand to Jordan to give the exact policy language and technical controls.

[02:41] Jordan (Redwood): We have a written policy: customer prompt/input and generated output are classified as customer data. For hosted and dedicated we persist request/response payloads for up to X days for debugging (default 30 days), configurable per contract. We do not include customer data in any model training datasets — that's explicitly prohibited by policy and enforcement. Logs used for model performance are synthetic/aggregate-only and never contain raw customer prompts. (slight hesitation)
[03:12] Taylor (HeliosHealth): When you say 'not used for training' is that a contractual guarantee? we need it in the DPA and SOC 2 mappings.

[03:19] Samir (Redwood): Yes we can provide contract language in the DPA: 'Redwood will not, without Customer's prior written consent, use Customer Data to train or improve models.' We also map that control in our SOC 2 evidence — we'll include the control IDs.
[03:35] Marcus (HeliosHealth): For PHI specifically, do you offer de-identification or automatic redaction? We cannot send raw PHI to a shared hosted endpoint without guarantees.

[03:45] Samir (Redwood): We offer several options: 1) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) so data never leaves customer's network; 2) Dedicated isolated tenancy where tenant data is logically separated and can be configured to not be persisted beyond processing; 3) Built-in PII/PHI redaction hooks — not perfect but we can run a model-based redaction step client-side or server-side before storage. We'll share our redaction guide and limitations.
[04:12] Priya (HeliosHealth): For the Dedicated option, is there an option to disable any request/response logging entirely?

[04:18] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, for Dedicated you can disable payload logging and only keep telemetry. For customers with strict compliance we also support never-writing payloads to disk and using in-memory processing with KMS-protected ephemeral keys.
[04:35] Riley (HeliosHealth): KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed keys (CMKs) from AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault?

[04:41] Samir (Redwood): We support BYOK via AWS KMS and have beta for GCP CMEK and Azure. The private offering can use an HSM-backed key store via our enterprise package. We'll include the KMS integration doc.
[04:55] Taylor (HeliosHealth): What about encryption in transit and at rest? and full disk encryption for ephemeral nodes?

[05:02] Jordan (Redwood): TLS 1.2+ in transit, and AES-256 at rest. Ephemeral nodes are disk-encrypted, and keys are rotated per our key rotation schedule. For Dedicated/Private you can bring your own key and rotate per your policy.
[05:30] Priya (HeliosHealth): Data residency: can we restrict region of processing and storage to EU or us-east only? we have data residency requirements for certain patient data.

[05:38] Alex (Redwood): Yes region pinning is available — hosted supports region selection and Dedicated/Private obviously allow strict control. We'll need to capture which datasets are EU vs US for compliance mapping.
[05:55] Marcus (HeliosHealth): How are service accounts and machine identities handled? we need mTLS between services and mutual auth for internal APIs.

[06:01] Jordan (Redwood): We authenticate service-to-service with mTLS, short-lived certificates, and use OIDC-backed service identities in our control plane. We'll provide architecture diagrams for that.
[06:15] Taylor (HeliosHealth): Can you outline your incident response and breach notification timelines? we have 72-hour obligations under our policies.

[06:21] Samir (Redwood): Our incident response SLA: initial ack within 1 hour for P1, notification to customers within 24 hours for confirmed breaches, full report within agreed timeframes. We can map to your 72-hour requirement and include it in the contract.
[06:40] Riley (HeliosHealth): For audits — do you allow for auditor access or read-only footprints for their assessments?

[06:46] Alex (Redwood): For enterprise deals we provide auditor access via a temporary read-only portal and provide necessary artifacts. For Private deployments auditors can be given direct network access per legal terms.

[07:00] Taylor (HeliosHealth): Ok thanks, that's helpful. Back to retention: you mentioned default 30 days — can that be reduced to zero for certain environments? we need ability to opt-out of retention entirely for specific endpoints.

[07:12] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — retention is configurable per-route. You can set a route to ephemeral mode (no persistence) or a short TTL; for Dedicated we can set TTL to zero as part of onboarding. We'll surface this in the API as 'persist: false'.
[07:28] Priya (HeliosHealth): If persist:false is set, does that affect debugging and support? how do you triage incidents?

[07:33] Samir (Redwood): It reduces our ability to debug payload-level issues. We recommend a short-term debug window where you temporarily enable retention and then revoke it. Alternatively, customers can stream request logs to their S3 for debugging so Redwood never retains them.

[07:52] Marcus (HeliosHealth): Regarding 'no training' — can you walk us through the technical controls preventing accidental inclusion in training data? is it purely policy or enforced at pipeline level?

[08:01] Jordan (Redwood): It's both. Policy forbids use of customer data for training. Technically, training data pipelines are separate and require explicit whitelisting and approvals. Access controls, audit logs, and automated checks flag any customer-data-like artifacts. Also, dataset ingestion for model updates is from curated corpora only.
[08:24] Taylor (HeliosHealth): Are there any telemetry or metadata fields that might leak PII (e.g., truncated prompts in monitoring)?

[08:31] Samir (Redwood): We scrub identifiable fields from telemetry and use hashed identifiers for session traces. There are telemetry knobs — for high-sensitivity customers we can reduce telemetry granularity.
[08:49] Alex (Redwood): I'll note that our SDKs also support client-side redaction hooks so you can redact before sending.
[09:00] Priya (HeliosHealth): Good. On legal — DPA and specific clause on no-training — can we get that language before we go to our counsel?
[09:07] Alex (Redwood): Yes we'll send a draft DPA with the no-training clause and data residency addendum.
[09:15] Riley (HeliosHealth): Do you have any prior customers in healthcare who did a PHI pilot? references would be helpful.
[09:21] Jordan (Redwood): We have a few healthcare customers on Dedicated/private plans — we'll redact references, but we can provide anonymized case studies and an architecture reference.
[09:35] Taylor (HeliosHealth): One more on deletion — if we delete data from Redwood, how do you guarantee it's purged from backups and logs?

[09:43] Samir (Redwood): Deletion policy: we support soft-delete and hard-delete. Hard-delete triggers expunge from primary stores; backups are retained per backup retention schedule (typically 30 days) but we support expedited purge for enterprise customers with attestations. We'll include the purge playbook.
[10:05] Priya (HeliosHealth): Are there SOC 2 control IDs that map to 'no-training' and 'data deletion'? we'll need those for our compliance matrix.
[10:12] Samir (Redwood): Yes — we'll map relevant controls and provide the SOC 2 testing points. Expect those in the pack.
[10:25] Alex (Redwood): Time check — we have about 35 minutes left, want to dive into a quick demo of route configs and retention settings? or save for follow-up technical pilot?
[10:33] Priya (HeliosHealth): Pilot please — we'd rather schedule a pilot to validate retention, redaction, and KMS flows.
[10:39] Alex (Redwood): Great. Samir/Jordan — what do we need to run a 2-week pilot?

[10:44] Jordan (Redwood): We'll need a small staging dataset, region preference, desired retention policy (persist:false vs TTL), and KMS details if using CMK. We'll provision a Dedicated tenant for pilot, or use a private VPC connector depending on your preference.
[10:59] Marcus (HeliosHealth): For initial test let's do Dedicated with persist:false and customer-managed key in us-east-1.
[11:05] Samir (Redwood): Noted. We'll provision and share onboarding docs; expect an SSO integration step as well.
[11:14] Taylor (HeliosHealth): Questions from my security team: how do you handle subcontractors and third-party processors?
[11:20] Alex (Redwood): We have a vendor management program and a list of subprocessors in the DPA. Third parties are contractually bound and monitored. We'll include the current subprocessor list.

[11:33] Priya (HeliosHealth): A couple of small asks: 1) a one-page data flow diagram showing where prompts go, where they're stored, and who can access them; 2) sample API call showing persist:false; 3) SOC2 certificate and DPA draft.
[11:46] Jordan (Redwood): We can provide all three. We'll also include the KMS integration guide and redaction playbook.
[11:58] Alex (Redwood): Ok let's recap and confirm next steps, then we'll open for any final questions.

[12:05] Alex (Redwood): Recap: Redwood to send SOC2 pack, DPA with no-training clause, KMS integration doc, data flow diagram, redaction guide, and provision a Dedicated pilot (persist:false, CMK in us-east-1). Customer to confirm pilot timeline and provide staging dataset and SSO admin contact.
[12:30] Priya (HeliosHealth): Sounds right. We'll target start of pilot next week pending internal approvals.
[12:36] Taylor (HeliosHealth): One last question — if we later decide to enable short-term retention for debugging, what's the process?
[12:42] Samir (Redwood): You'd create a debug request via the console or API for a defined window; all changes are audited. We'll also provide a governance playbook for debug windows.
[12:55] Riley (HeliosHealth): Thanks everyone — no further questions from my side.
[13:00] Alex (Redwood): Great thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts within 24 hours and schedule the pilot kickoff.
[13:07] (call ends)
[45:00] (actual meeting duration recorded as 48 minutes in metadata)
